target_boundary: Explain the Arcanum goal spell as a Craft-backed, fail-closed routing process: how it reads a frontier, classifies risk, routes eligible nodes, audits receipts, stages deltas, waits for approval, and decides when to stop.

reader_contract.target_public: A reader who wants to understand what the goal spell will do before trusting it with a repository work graph.
assumed_knowledge: The reader knows that a repository may have tasks, blockers, and next moves.
The reader can read a simple process graph with stop branches.
reader_contract.reader_reward: The reader can explain how goal decides the next step, why it stops, and what evidence must exist before ledger changes are promoted.

must_start_with: Start from the plain problem: a work graph can keep going forever or mutate too early unless a control loop stops on uncertainty.
Introduce goal as a router before naming its internal artifacts.
must_not_start_with: Do not start with the output contract or telemetry fields.
Do not imply goal executes protected work directly.
opening_contract.failure_message: If the page makes goal look like an autonomous mutator instead of a fail-closed router, it fails the reader contract.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: A router for a Craft-backed work graph.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: It decides which work can continue, which work needs an owner, and which work must stop before mutation.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Do not treat goal as the owner of delegated sigils or as permission to mutate the ledger directly.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: The currently visible set of open next moves, blockers, gaps, or candidate SWUs.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: Goal can only decide from a bounded frontier snapshot; if the source cannot be identified safely, it blocks.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Do not assume memory or broad repository intuition is the frontier.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: A safety label for a node, from low-risk read-only work to protected work.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: Unknown work defaults to protected, so unclear or dangerous actions stop before execution.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Do not downgrade a node just because the user wants progress.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: A validated handoff plan naming owner, technique, inputs, receipt, gate, and fallback.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: Goal routes eligible work but does not redefine the delegated owner's behavior.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Do not treat a route as success; it only frames delegated work.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: Terminal evidence returned by the delegated owner after a routed node is handled or blocked.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: Goal cannot audit or stage progress unless every delegated lane is joined and terminal.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Do not close a node from vibes, partial work, or an open lane.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: A proposed ledger change held outside the active ledger until approval.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: It keeps useful progress reviewable without silently changing source state.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Do not write active ledger rows directly from a goal round.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: An explicit, durable permission record for applying a staged batch.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: Promotion is blocked until the exact batch has approval and a decision record.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Ambient approval or general enthusiasm is not enough.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: When unsure, stop or block instead of guessing permission.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: This is the main safety posture: unknown source, unknown risk, missing receipt, audit veto, and missing approval all stop movement.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Fail-closed is not a failure of the agent; it is the designed safety behavior.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: As a newcomer, I want the page to start with the practical problem.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: Goal exists because a work graph needs a loop that can continue useful work without mutating protected state too early.
layer_reader_outcomes.because_it_matters_for: trusting the tool's purpose before learning its local vocabulary.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: As a working reader, I want to know the invariant rules.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: Goal is a router, default-denies unknown work, stages deltas, and promotes only after explicit approval.
layer_reader_outcomes.because_it_matters_for: predicting behavior before running the spell.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: As a working reader, I want the parts of the loop named plainly.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: Frontier, risk classifier, dispatch route, receipt, audit, staged delta, approval, promotion, gap discovery, and telemetry are separate parts.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: As a reviewer, I want to know which parts depend on each other inside the spell.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: Risk classification feeds route selection; receipts feed audit; audit feeds staged deltas; approval gates promotion.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: As a reviewer, I want to know what goal depends on but does not own.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: Craft owns ledger apply, Dispatch Spec validates route shape, Task Session owns bounded execution, Decision Gate owns approval records, and observability records signals.
layer_reader_outcomes.because_it_matters_for: avoiding the mistake of blaming goal for delegated owner behavior.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: As a newcomer, I want to follow the main path and its stop branches.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: Goal binds scope, reads frontier, classifies risk, routes eligible work, joins receipts, audits, stages, waits for approval, then promotes or stops.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: As a maintainer, I want to know what happens over a full round.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: A round moves from bind to read to classify to dispatch to audit to stage to approval to promotion, or to bounded gap discovery when the frontier is empty.
layer_reader_outcomes.because_it_matters_for: knowing where the loop can terminate.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: As an operator, I want the stop conditions visible.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: Goal stops on source-authority ambiguity, protected or unknown risk, route failure, missing receipt, audit veto, direct ledger writes, missing approval, budget ceiling, and promotion without experiment evidence.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: As a scanner, I want the graph and tables to explain different slices.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: The graph shows the control spine, the switchboard shows decision questions, and the stop wall shows why a run returns STOP or BLOCK.

evidence: arcanum/spells/goal/README.md says goal drives a Craft-backed work graph through an autonomous, fail-closed control loop.
arcanum/spells/goal/README.md says goal is a router and does not execute protected work directly or mutate the source ledger without approved staged proposal.
inference: The best reader on-ramp is: goal is a cautious dispatcher for a work graph, not an all-powerful executor.

evidence: arcanum/spells/goal/decision-profile.schema sets unknown_action to stop and default_tier to T3 in the neutral default.
arcanum/spells/goal/decision-profile.schema lists protected operations: active-ledger-mutation, commit, push, pull-request, publication, ci, network, and destructive-shell.
arcanum/spells/goal/decision-profile.schema requires explicit-token promotion mode and a decision record.
inference: The practical decision model is default-deny: read-only and staged-proposal lanes can proceed; protected actions need explicit approval.

evidence: arcanum/spells/goal/README.md lists Goal bind, Read frontier, Classify risk, Select owner and technique, Dispatch and receipt join, Audit gate, Stage delta, Batch approval, Promote, and Gap discovery as execution phases.
arcanum/spells/goal/README.md lists Frontier snapshot, Dispatch route, Execution receipt, Staged delta, Framed batch diff, Decision record, and Spell telemetry signal as handoff artifacts.
inference: These phases and artifacts can be drawn as separate components because each has different entry evidence, owner boundary, and stop behavior.

evidence: arcanum/spells/goal/README.md control spine orders frontier read, risk classification, Dispatch Spec route selection, delegated receipt collection, audit, staged delta, and explicit approval before promotion.
arcanum/spells/goal/runtime/goal_loop.py builds result stop_reason source-authority when binding source fails and t3-node when T3 reasons appear.
inference: The loop is easier to diagnose if each phase exposes the artifact it needs from the previous phase.

evidence: arcanum/spells/goal/README.md says arcana/craft reads frontier state and applies approved ledger batches.
arcanum/spells/goal/README.md says formulae/dispatch-spec validates per-node owner, technique, and receipt routes.
arcanum/spells/goal/README.md says arcana/task-session executes one bounded node or SWU with done criteria and validation.
arcanum/spells/goal/README.md says arcana/decision-gate records durable approval or blocker decisions.
arcanum/spells/goal/README.md says observability capabilities emit spell-level telemetry and post-run signals.
inference: Goal's decision quality depends on these owners being present, but goal does not own their internal behavior.

evidence: arcanum/spells/goal/README.md lists the control spine and cross-cutting guards.
arcanum/spells/goal/README.md says unknown risk, missing approval, audit veto, and missing terminal closeout stop the loop.
arcanum/spells/goal/runtime/goal_loop.py classifies protected terms and blocked/protected status as T3.
arcanum/spells/goal/runtime/goal_loop.py evaluate_approval_boundary blocks ambient approval and token mismatch, and holds missing approval.
inference: A single graph with green continue edges and red stop edges best answers how goal makes decisions.

evidence: arcanum/spells/goal/README.md says gap discovery runs only after the active frontier is empty and the caller opts in.
arcanum/spells/goal/runtime/goal_loop.py run_gap_discovery blocks when frontier is not empty, stops at budget ceiling, and dedupes candidate gaps.
arcanum/spells/goal/validation/results/fixture-report.md shows gap_discovery passed with dedupe-complete and budget_stop stopped with budget-ceiling.
inference: Gap discovery is not automatic expansion of work; it is a bounded proposal queue after the active frontier is done.

evidence: arcanum/spells/goal/README.md failure policy lists protected risk, missing human gates, audit veto, missing closeout, direct mutation, public profile leakage, and promotion without Experiment Harness evidence as stop or block cases.

arcanum/spells/goal/validation/results/fixture-report.md shows protected_frontier STOP t3-node, missing_source BLOCK source-authority, audit_veto block, ambient_approval blocked, and budget_stop STOP budget-ceiling.
inference: The useful question for operators is not 'why did goal fail?' but 'which designed stop protected the graph?'

evidence: arcanum/arcana/x-ray/SKILL.md says L0 static HTML/SVG is the default proof path.
arcanum/arcana/x-ray/library/patterns.yml includes process-branch, dependency-boundary, lifecycle-stack, and evidence-inference-split patterns.
arcanum/arcana/x-ray/library/components.yml includes shape.node, connector.arrow, connector.branch, connector.feedback-loop, chart.timeline-strip, and chart.risk-matrix.
inference: Use process-branch for decisions, dependency-boundary for owners, lifecycle-stack for round states, and evidence-inference-split for the stop wall.
